S121-01. The opening passage demands that the germ from (D_d,x) to (X,a) be the intersection of the inserted branch germs D_x^i and that the intersection be transverse. This is an axiom stated on the page; no construction or general consistency proof was supplied or checked here. The literal q. bien sûr que remains, without smoothing its syntax.

S121-02. The two open drawings and their shared labels are offered as cases allowed by the axiomatic description but not captured by the datum of a divisor on X. This general claim is carried as background: no definition of all preceding axioms, no global divisor comparison, and no test of transversality at the drawn upper contact were reconstructed. The ambiguous D subscript is not resolved from the claim.

The curve drawing is encoded in TikZ. Its two alternatives, the written ou, the free ends, the self-crossing strokes, the very faint interrupted right return of the lower drawing, and the two short ticks on its dark upper-right section are retained. Those ticks are not promoted to full arrowheads. The vertical bracket-like leader beside the normalization note is also drawn. Opacity and line width distinguish the pale surviving segment; they do not assert its intended completion.

S121-03. Formula (183) constructs a local lattice T_d using the symmetric-group action on Z^d. A conditional local calculation was checked: permutation matrices have integral inverses and satisfy the group law, so local trivializations of an S_d-torsor yield locally constant Z^d fibres with permutation transition maps. This does not verify the existence or all hypotheses of the torsor from earlier pages.

S121-04. The page calls the relative group analytic and, with the literal parenthetical et =, algebraic. Formula (184) is copied with its visible D_d^d. That high d differs from the exclamation in (183); the expected associated-torus construction would invite comparison with D_d^!, but expectation is not used to replace the clear high letter. Global algebraic representability and descent are carried as background, not proved in this reading.

S121-05. A limited fibre check supports the conventional interpretation of the final invariant: if the complex analytic fibre is (C*)^d, the coordinatewise homotopy z -> z|z|^{-t}, for 0<=t<=1, retracts it onto (S^1)^d. Its fundamental group is Z^d and its first homology is the abelianization, also Z^d; coordinate permutations act by the corresponding permutation matrices. This identifies the conventional local lattice conditionally. It does not settle whether the written Π-like sign is upper or lower case, nor verify all global hypotheses.

H's editorial end note and end-document command are not manuscript ink and are not treated as missing source text. The source itself has a dark separate terminal point after fibres. H's broad drawing caption is evaluated only for its explicit closed-curve reading, not transcribed as words on the page.

Cross-page root review of the existing (184), (188), and (190) crops confirms that the D_d base in (184) is lower than m. Grouped subscripting preserves the two levels; this does not alter the named group or base.
